scenario: AITA for calling out professor for making fun of me in class? | Backstory real quick: (20M) I’m a ginger (orange hair, freckles, and I wear glasses as well) and have been made fun of for it for basically my whole life; I’ve had to hear just about every term in the book from firehead, red, carrot top, firecrotch, etc. All of it really pisses me off but I try to keep it to myself b/c god forbid people think I “can’t take a joke”. On several different occasions a professor I had in one of my tech classes this past semester made “jokes” about it. Second week of the year he says after forgetting my name “I’ll remember you, you’re the guy with no soul” and third week “Oh that’s right EverywhereForever, you’re the ginger with no soul”. Most of the class laughed, I was pissed and too embarrassed to say anything. It stopped for awhile after that though. Towards the end of the semester though he did it again, and I straight lost my cool and said “It’s not funny. How would you like it if I called you baldy every day I walked in?” He didn’t say anything, class was quiet and he just continued with his lesson. I left for the bathroom b/c I was embarrassed and just got it together and walked back into class like nothing happened. The next day a kid talks to me outside class and said I was a dick about it and I just shrugged. Far be it from me to think something as arbitrary as my fucking hair color would be beyond juvenile and insulting remarks in college. AITA for the way I had reacted to this? This was mostly younger kids who had just graduated last year I think so I guess it may have influence on how they think but I wouldn’t expect it from a professor.

Let me break this down step by step. First, I need to understand the situation. I'm a 20-year-old imaging student with orange hair, freckles, and glasses. I've been made fun of for my appearance my whole life. The professor in one of my tech classes made jokes about my hair color and soullessness. The first time was in the second week, and then again towards the end of the semester. The class laughed, which made me really upset and embarrassed. I kept my cool at first but eventually snapped and told the professor it wasn't funny, comparing it to someone calling him bald every day. He didn't respond, and class went on. The next day, a student called me a dick for reacting that way, and I just shrugged it off. Now, I'm wondering if I overreacted. Is it wrong to stand up for myself, or should I have just let it go? I'm also considering the professor's behavior. Should a professor be making jokes about a student's appearance, especially in a way that could be hurtful? And how do I handle the student who criticized my reaction? I think about why I reacted the way I did. I've been dealing with this kind of teasing for so long, and it's really hurtful. The professor's comments were in a professional setting, which makes it worse because I expect respect there. When I snapped, I was trying to make him understand how it felt, but maybe I should have handled it differently. On the other hand, the student who called me a dick might not understand how much it affected me. They might think it's just a joke, but for me, it's personal. I wonder if I should have talked to the professor privately instead of confronting him in front of the class. That might have been a better approach, but I was too upset at the moment. I also think about whether it's right to hold a professor to a higher standard. They should know better than to make such jokes, especially in a classroom setting. It's not just about my feelings; it's about creating a respectful environment for all students. In the end, I feel like I had a right to stand up for myself, but maybe the way I did it could have been handled more calmly. However, I was in the moment and reacting to years of being teased. I don't think I'm AITA for feeling upset and speaking up, even if my reaction was a bit strong.
